# Validation rule catalog

30 hand-curated rules. Each fires on a known Razorpay integration mistake and points at the canonical doc that explains the fix. Severity `error` means we're confident; `warning` means likely-bug; `info` is "you might want to know."

Run:

```bash
validate_razorpay_code(code, language?, concern?)
```

Or from a code snippet via your MCP-aware editor.

## Rules by concern

## `amount_handling` (1 rule)

### RZP003 — Amount looks like rupees, not paise

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `amount_handling` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Razorpay expects amounts in the smallest unit (paise for INR). A ₹100 order is `amount: 10000`. Multiply rupee values by 100 before sending.

**Fix:**

```
const amountInPaise = Math.round(rupees * 100);
await razorpay.orders.create({ amount: amountInPaise, currency: 'INR' });
```

**Citation:** [`api/orders/create`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/orders/create/) — All Razorpay amounts are in the smallest currency unit. ₹100 must be sent as `10000`, not `100`.

## `capture` (2 rules)

### RZP007 — `payment_capture: 0` without a follow-up capture call

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `capture` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Setting `payment_capture: 0` puts the payment in 'authorized' state. Without an explicit capture call within 5 days the funds are released back to the customer.

**Fix:**

```
// Either auto-capture:
await razorpay.orders.create({ amount, currency, payment_capture: 1 });
// Or manual capture, with a follow-up:
await razorpay.payments.capture(paymentId, amount, currency);
```

**Citation:** [`api/payments/capture`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/payments/capture/) — When `payment_capture` is 0 the payment is only authorized — you must call capture explicitly within the auto-void window.

### RZP026 — Capture scheduled past the 5-day auto-void window

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `capture` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

If you must capture later, enable late-authorization on your account. Otherwise, capture within 5 days of authorize — preferably immediately on payment.captured webhook.

**Fix:**

```
// On payment.authorized webhook, capture within minutes:
await razorpay.payments.capture(paymentId, amount, currency);
```

**Citation:** [`payments/payments/late-authorisation`](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payments/late-authorisation/) — Payments auto-void after 5 days. Capturing past that window requires the late-authorization flow.

## `currency` (2 rules)

### RZP012 — Order and payment have different currencies

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `currency` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Pass the same `currency` to both orders.create and any subsequent payment/refund call. Mixed currencies cause downstream capture failures and reconciliation drift.

**Fix:**

```
const currency = 'INR';
const order = await razorpay.orders.create({ amount, currency });
// ... later
await razorpay.payments.fetch(paymentId); // currency already locked to the order
```

**Citation:** [`api/orders`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/orders/) — The currency on a payment must match the currency of its parent order; otherwise the capture will reject.

### RZP022 — Currency code is not uppercase ISO 4217

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `currency` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `regex`

The Razorpay API accepts and expects uppercase ISO 4217 codes. Lowercase values are silently coerced in some SDKs and rejected in others — keep them uppercase to be safe.

**Fix:**

```
currency: 'INR' // not 'inr'
```

**Citation:** [`api`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/) — Currency codes follow ISO 4217 — three uppercase letters (e.g., INR, USD).

## `idempotency` (3 rules)

### RZP008 — Refund created without an Idempotency-Key header

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `idempotency` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Refunds are not naturally idempotent. Without a key, a network retry can refund twice. Generate a per-attempt UUID and send it as `Idempotency-Key`.

**Fix:**

```
await razorpay.payments.refund(paymentId, {
  amount,
  notes,
}, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': crypto.randomUUID() } });
```

**Citation:** [`api/refunds/normal-refunds-idempotent`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/refunds/normal-refunds-idempotent/) — Pass `Idempotency-Key` so a retried request doesn't issue two refunds for the same payment.

### RZP021 — Webhook handler does not dedupe repeat events

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `idempotency` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Razorpay retries webhook deliveries until it gets a 2xx, and may deliver duplicates. Persist each `event.id` after first processing and short-circuit subsequent deliveries of the same id.

**Fix:**

```
// reject duplicates before doing the work
const inserted = await db.events.insertIfMissing({ event_id: event.id });
if (!inserted) return res.status(200).end(); // already handled
// ... process event ...
```

**Citation:** [`webhooks/best-practices`](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/best-practices/) — Razorpay re-delivers webhook events; your handler must be idempotent on event id.

### RZP027 — Refund created without a `speed` parameter

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `idempotency` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Without `speed`, refund settlement falls back to 'normal' (5–7 days). Most consumer-facing flows want 'optimum' (fast where supported, normal otherwise) — pass it explicitly.

**Fix:**

```
await razorpay.payments.refund(paymentId, { amount, speed: 'optimum' });
```

**Citation:** [`api/refunds/create-instant`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/refunds/create-instant/) — Specify `speed` ('normal', 'optimum', or 'instant') so the refund's settlement time is explicit.

## `key_safety` (5 rules)

### RZP005 — Hardcoded live API key

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `key_safety` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `regex`

Live keys grant production write access. Move them to environment variables and rotate any key that has touched source control.

**Fix:**

```
const razorpay = new Razorpay({
  key_id: process.env.RZP_KEY_ID,
  key_secret: process.env.RZP_KEY_SECRET,
});
```

**Citation:** [`payments/dashboard/account-settings/api-keys`](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/api-keys/) — Live keys must never be committed; rotate immediately if exposed.

### RZP006 — Hardcoded test API key

**Severity:** 🔵 info · **Concern:** `key_safety` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `regex`

Test keys are lower-risk than live, but still account-scoped. For shared repos, read them from env so you can rotate without a code change.

**Fix:**

```
const razorpay = new Razorpay({
  key_id: process.env.RZP_KEY_ID,
  key_secret: process.env.RZP_KEY_SECRET,
});
```

**Citation:** [`payments/dashboard/account-settings/api-keys`](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/api-keys/) — Even test keys leak account routing info; prefer env vars in shared code.

### RZP019 — Test API key paired with production env detection

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `key_safety` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Wiring a test key into a production-only branch silently breaks payments in production. Pick credentials by environment, not by string match.

**Fix:**

```
const isProd = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production';
const keyId  = isProd ? process.env.RZP_LIVE_KEY_ID  : process.env.RZP_TEST_KEY_ID;
const secret = isProd ? process.env.RZP_LIVE_SECRET : process.env.RZP_TEST_SECRET;
```

**Citation:** [`payments/dashboard`](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/) — Production code must use live (`rzp_live_…`) credentials; test keys won't capture real money.

### RZP023 — key_secret referenced in client-side code

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `key_safety` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Anything bundled to the browser is public. Sign the order/payment server-side, ship only `key_id` to the client, and let the checkout SDK do the rest.

**Fix:**

```
// server: returns { keyId: process.env.RZP_KEY_ID, orderId } to the client
// client:
new Razorpay({ key: keyId, order_id: orderId, /* no secret */ });
```

**Citation:** [`payments/dashboard/account-settings/api-keys`](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/api-keys/) — `key_secret` must remain server-side; the browser only ever sees `key_id`.

### RZP030 — Outdated Razorpay SDK declared in package.json

**Severity:** 🔵 info · **Concern:** `key_safety` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `regex`

The pinned Razorpay SDK is older than the current major. Upgrade to the latest major to get current API surface (UPI 2.0, recurring v3, latest webhook event shapes).

**Fix:**

```
"razorpay": "^2.9.0"
```

**Citation:** [`api/changelog`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/changelog/) — Upgrade to the latest major to get new payment method support and bug fixes.

## `order_flow` (4 rules)

### RZP004 — payments.create called without a preceding orders.create

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `order_flow` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

An order is the contract Razorpay verifies against. Creating a payment without one means there's nothing to settle the payment to, and signature verification has no canonical id to sign.

**Fix:**

```
const order = await razorpay.orders.create({ amount, currency: 'INR' });
// pass order.id to the client; client uses it during checkout
// payments are then bound to order.id end-to-end
```

**Citation:** [`api/orders/create`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/orders/create/) — Always create an Order first; the payment that follows is bound to that order's id and currency.

### RZP017 — `notes` value exceeds the 256-character limit

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `order_flow` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Razorpay rejects notes whose values exceed 256 characters. For longer payloads, store them in your DB and put just the reference id (or a short hash) in notes.

**Fix:**

```
notes: { internal_ref: 'order_42' } // short string; long context lives in your DB
```

**Citation:** [`api/orders/create`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/orders/create/#notes) — Each value in `notes` is capped at 256 characters.

### RZP018 — `receipt` field exceeds the 40-character limit

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `order_flow` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

The order create endpoint rejects receipts longer than 40 chars. Use a short, unique tag (e.g., your internal order short-id).

**Fix:**

```
receipt: `r_${shortId}` // ≤ 40 chars
```

**Citation:** [`api/orders/create`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/orders/create/#receipt) — The `receipt` field is capped at 40 characters.

### RZP029 — Receipt derived from time only — collision risk

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `order_flow` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Time-only receipts collide under concurrency. Mix in a random token (UUID, nanoid, secrets.token_hex) so duplicates are impossible.

**Fix:**

```
receipt: `r_${Date.now()}_${crypto.randomUUID().slice(0,8)}`
```

**Citation:** [`api/orders/create`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/orders/create/) — Receipts must be unique per order. Two requests in the same millisecond will collide.

## `payment_methods` (5 rules)

### RZP013 — Subscription created with `addons` but no validation

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `payment_methods` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Razorpay rejects ill-formed addons with 400, but the failure path is awkward to recover from after collecting customer payment intent. Validate at the boundary.

**Fix:**

```
const addons = AddonSchema.array().parse(rawAddons);
await razorpay.subscriptions.create({ plan_id, addons, total_count });
```

**Citation:** [`payments/subscriptions`](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/) — Validate addon shape (item.amount, item.currency, quantity) before passing to subscriptions.create — the API will 400 on malformed entries.

### RZP014 — UPI intent payment without callback_url

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `payment_methods` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Without `callback_url` the user is stranded in their UPI app after paying — your code never learns the outcome and the user thinks the merchant lost the transaction.

**Fix:**

```
await razorpay.payments.create({
  method: 'upi', flow: 'intent',
  callback_url: 'https://example.com/orders/' + orderId + '/return',
});
```

**Citation:** [`payments/payment-methods/upi`](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/) — UPI intent flow needs `callback_url` so the PSP app returns control to your page after authorization.

### RZP015 — Payment Link created without expire_by

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `payment_methods` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Open-ended Payment Links are a foot-gun: a customer can pay a stale link and force you to refund. Set `expire_by` to a sensible TTL (e.g., 24h).

**Fix:**

```
await razorpay.paymentLink.create({
  amount, currency: 'INR',
  expire_by: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 24 * 60 * 60,
});
```

**Citation:** [`api/payments/payment-links/create-standard`](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/payments/payment-links/create-standard/) — Pass `expire_by` (Unix epoch seconds) so abandoned links can't be paid days later, after price/inventory has changed.

### RZP024 — Partner integration without `X-Razorpay-Account` header

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `payment_methods` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Without `X-Razorpay-Account` the request operates on the partner account, not the submerchant. Money flows the wrong way and reconciliation breaks.

**Fix:**

```
await fetch('https://api.razorpay.com/v1/orders', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'X-Razorpay-Account': 'acc_' + subMerchantId, /* auth */ },
  body: JSON.stringify({ amount, currency: 'INR' }),
});
```

**Citation:** [`partners`](https://razorpay.com/docs/partners/) — Partner-scoped requests must carry `X-Razorpay-Account: acc_<sub_merchant_id>` — otherwise the request runs on the partner's account.

### RZP025 — Recurring auth amount above ₹15000 with `recurring=preferred`

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `payment_methods` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

RBI guidelines cap recurring auth at ₹15,000 (1500000 paise) without additional factor authentication. Higher amounts require the explicit AFA path.

**Fix:**

```
auth_amount: 100, // typical ₹1 token charge for mandate setup
```

**Citation:** [`announcements/rbi-card-mandate-guidelines/recurring-payments`](https://razorpay.com/docs/announcements/rbi-card-mandate-guidelines/recurring-payments/) — RBI card-mandate guidelines cap the auth amount at ₹15,000. Use higher values only with explicit AFA flow.

## `pci_compliance` (2 rules)

### RZP009 — CVV being stored or logged server-side

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `pci_compliance` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

CVV must only be passed to Razorpay (or your gateway) at the moment of authorization. Never save it, never write it to logs, never include it in an exception trace.

**Fix:**

```
// pass to checkout / tokenize via Razorpay; do not persist
const { token } = await razorpay.tokens.create({ /* card data, including cvv */ });
// store only `token.id` server-side
```

**Citation:** [`security/checklist`](https://razorpay.com/docs/security/checklist/) — PCI-DSS prohibits storing or logging the card's CVV/CVC under any circumstance.

### RZP010 — Full PAN being stored or logged server-side

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `pci_compliance` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Storing PANs (or even logging them) puts you in PCI-DSS Level 1 scope. Tokenize once via Razorpay and reference the token thereafter; the PAN never lands in your systems.

**Fix:**

```
// Razorpay returns a token id you can store and re-charge against
const token = await razorpay.tokens.create({ /* card payload */ });
db.cards.insert({ user_id, token_id: token.id }); // no PAN
```

**Citation:** [`security/checklist`](https://razorpay.com/docs/security/checklist/) — Full PANs may not be stored unencrypted. Use Razorpay tokenization and persist only the token reference.

## `webhook_handler` (2 rules)

### RZP011 — Webhook URL uses a non-standard port

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `webhook_handler` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `regex`

Razorpay's outbound webhook caller refuses non-standard ports — your endpoint will never be hit. Front the handler with a load balancer or reverse proxy on 443.

**Fix:**

```
// public URL must be on 443 (or 80 plaintext)
https://api.example.com/razorpay/webhook
```

**Citation:** [`webhooks/setup-edit-payments`](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/setup-edit-payments/) — Razorpay only delivers webhooks to ports 80 (http) and 443 (https). Custom ports are silently dropped.

### RZP020 — Webhook handler returns 4xx/5xx in the success path

**Severity:** 🟡 warning · **Concern:** `webhook_handler` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

Razorpay treats any non-2xx as a delivery failure and retries with exponential backoff. Always 200/204 once the event is accepted; do downstream work asynchronously.

**Fix:**

```
// 1. verify signature
// 2. enqueue job
// 3. ack
return res.status(200).end();
```

**Citation:** [`webhooks/best-practices`](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/best-practices/) — Acknowledge with a 2xx as soon as you've received the event; non-2xx triggers retries that compound load.

## `webhook_signature` (4 rules)

### RZP001 — Webhook signature computed over JSON.stringify(req.body)

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `webhook_signature` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `regex`

Razorpay signs the exact bytes it sent. JSON.stringify produces a different byte sequence (key order, whitespace), so the HMAC will never match. Capture the raw body before any JSON parser runs.

**Fix:**

```
// Express: express.raw({ type: 'application/json' })
const expected = crypto
  .createHmac('sha256', process.env.RZP_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
  .update(req.rawBody) // raw bytes, not JSON.stringify(req.body)
  .digest('hex');
```

**Citation:** [`webhooks/validate-test`](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/validate-test/) — Compute the HMAC over the raw request body bytes, not over a re-serialized JSON object.

### RZP002 — Webhook signature compared with `==`/`===` instead of timing-safe equal

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `webhook_signature` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `heuristic`

String equality short-circuits on the first mismatched byte, leaking signature timing. Use the language's constant-time primitive.

**Fix:**

```
const sigBuf = Buffer.from(req.headers['x-razorpay-signature'] ?? '', 'hex');
const expBuf = Buffer.from(expected, 'hex');
if (sigBuf.length !== expBuf.length || !crypto.timingSafeEqual(sigBuf, expBuf)) {
  return res.status(400).end();
}
```

**Citation:** [`webhooks/validate-test`](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/validate-test/) — Use a constant-time comparison so an attacker cannot learn the secret from timing.

### RZP016 — Payment signature concatenation in the wrong order

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `webhook_signature` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `regex`

Razorpay's signature contract is `order_id|payment_id`. Reversing the parts produces a different HMAC, so the verification fails (or worse, succeeds on adversary-controlled inputs).

**Fix:**

```
const body = razorpay_order_id + "|" + razorpay_payment_id;
const expected = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(body).digest('hex');
```

**Citation:** [`webhooks/validate-test`](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/validate-test/) — Sign `${razorpay_order_id}|${razorpay_payment_id}` — order id first.

### RZP028 — Webhook secret read from request input

**Severity:** 🔴 error · **Concern:** `webhook_signature` · **Languages:** all SDKs · **Detector:** `regex`

Reading the secret from the incoming request defeats the entire signature mechanism — the caller can supply any secret and pass verification.

**Fix:**

```
const secret = process.env.RZP_WEBHOOK_SECRET; // configured once, server-side
```

**Citation:** [`webhooks/setup-edit-payments`](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/setup-edit-payments/) — Store the webhook secret as a server-side environment variable; never accept it from the request.
